title: A Failover counts as an oral prescription and needs no follow-up
rule_summary: Under 105 CMR 721.020(G) a Failover SHALL BE CONSIDERED AN ORAL PRESCRIPTION and SHALL NOT REQUIRE a written or electronic follow-up prescription, provided all three conditions hold: the prescription contains everything M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20(a) requires except the practitioner's signature and is immediately entered into a compliant electronic pharmacy system or otherwise reduced to writing by the dispensing pharmacist; if the prescribing practitioner is not known to the dispensing pharmacist, that pharmacist makes a reasonable good faith effort to determine the Failover was issued by a prescribing practitioner; and the prescription is NOT FOR AN ADDITIONAL DRUG as defined in 105 CMR 700.001. Under 105 CMR 721.040(C) an electronic prescription transmitted by other means is invalid except in the event of a Failover verified under 721.020(G).
exam_relevance: Tests the one route by which a Massachusetts oral controlled-substance prescription escapes the follow-up duty, and the additional-drug condition candidates miss.

authority.name: Failover treated as an oral prescription

exceptions: The three conditions in 105 CMR 721.020(G)(1)-(3) are conjunctive; failing any one leaves the ordinary follow-up duty in place.
A Failover for an Additional Drug does not qualify, so the follow-up duty continues to apply to it.
common_confusions: Treating every technological failure as a Failover without the three conditions.
Assuming the additional-drug carve-out is a formality rather than a condition that defeats the exception.
verification_notes: 105 CMR 721.020(G) and 721.040(C) read verbatim in the current official publication dated 9/27/24 on 2026-09-10, while building the Massachusetts oral-prescription section. Independent audit still required.
